track2.body:
**Track 2 Development: new scoring rule, updated texts and renamed units, from 6 October 2026 at 20:11 UTC**

Hi everyone. From 6 October 2026 at 20:11 UTC, the Track 2 Development board uses an updated scoring rule, your agent reads updated practice texts, and twenty practice units have new ids. Here is what changes and what it means for you.

**How a card is scored**
- Each component of a card's composite (marginal CRPS, joint variogram, tail) is now divided by **the error the text-blind baseline M0 expects to make on that card**. That divisor is computed exactly from the card's inputs, as `docs/M0-BASELINE.md` §5 describes.
- A score of 1.0 now means an error equal to the error M0 expects of itself. Lower is better, as before.
- **The cap and the failure value are both 8.0** (they were 4.0). A card's score is clipped at 8.0, and a card that is not scored counts as 8.0 and stays in the average.
- The scorer code, the card components and their weights are unchanged. The Final uses the same rule.

**Your earlier runs**
- Each of your finished Track 2 Development runs uploaded before 6 October 2026 at 20:11 UTC has been re-scored **under the new rule**, from the outputs it had already produced (nothing was re-run, and no upload was used).
- The board at agenthon.net shows the re-scored values, so every entry there is on one scale. The new values are not comparable with the ones shown before.
- Your CodaBench "My submissions" page keeps the old numbers for those earlier runs. The board is the place to compare.
- Runs uploaded from 6 October 2026 at 20:11 UTC on are scored under the new rule directly.
- Uploads made during the switch, between 20:11 UTC on 6 October and 00:22 UTC on 7 October, waited in "Submitting" and were then released to run under the new rule.
- If one of your earlier runs shows no score on the board, tell us here and we will look.

**The board**
- A labelled row, **"Reference forecaster M0"**, shows M0's own score under the same rule. It is unranked, it is not a team, and it does not count in the ranks or the paging.
- The board did not refresh, for any track, from 20:11 UTC on 6 October to 02:58 UTC on 7 October while the re-scored values were prepared.

**Renamed units**

Twenty practice units have new ids that name the event and the date. The unit directory, `[task].id`, the `card_id` in `forecast_spec.json` and `text/corpus_index.json`, and the manifest's `unit_id` change. Targets and panels are the same, and the text updates below apply to these units as to every other practice unit. If your code keys anything by unit id (caches, per-unit settings, notes), please update it.

**Updated texts**
- Every practice unit's text corpus has new documents, the units on the Development board included: decisions of the card's target central bank, documents of the event the card is built around, and speeches on unrelated topics, which are there on purpose. One misdated speech is removed from four COVID-era cards.
- On some practice cards, the title, `[metadata].description`, the "Text corpus role" paragraph or the `t2c-` catalog name is reworded.
- Targets and panels do not change. Runs uploaded from 6 October 2026 at 20:11 UTC on read the new texts, so a text-using agent's outputs on these units can change: a run from before the switch and one from after it are on one scale, but were given different texts.
- The CHANGELOG describes these changes.

**Card format**
- `[metadata].difficulty` and `[metadata].design_note` are **no longer part of the card format**.
- No card in `units/` or `templates/card.toml` carries them. The cards evaluated on CodaBench don't, and Final input cards won't. `.github/validate_units.py` refuses a card that does.
- If your code reads either key, please drop it.

**Local tools and docs** (this repository's `main`, commit `60509df`; please pull)
- The toolkit pin is now **`v2.6.0`**: CI, the README install lines, the `Dockerfile` and the guide links. `qfbench2 card validate` from `v2.6.0` accepts a card without `[metadata].difficulty`. To update a local install:
  ```
  pip install "qfbench2-common[data] @ git+https://github.com/Agenthon-2026/Agenthon2026-public.git@v2.6.0#subdirectory=common"
  ```
- The new pin changes nothing in how your submission runs on CodaBench.
- These docs describe the new rule: `docs/M0-BASELINE.md`, `docs/CONCEPTS.md`, the README and `baselines/README.md`.
- The worked examples in `docs/CATEGORIES.md` are updated.
- The CHANGELOG's Unreleased section has the details of every change above.

Questions are welcome here, as always.

— The Agenthon 2026 organizers

**Track 2 Final: how it's ranked and when results come**

We've settled how the Track 2 Final is ranked, so that no team can know any Final outcome when it uploads. Where the README, `docs/CATEGORIES.md`, the website, the CodaBench pages or an earlier notice says otherwise for Track 2, this notice replaces it; the changes are listed at the end.

**Your upload: unchanged.** You make your one Final upload any time from **13 October 12:00 UTC** until **25 October 23:59 AoE** (26 October 11:59 UTC), as published.

**In the window: a check run.** Your upload runs once on sealed cards we prepared before the window, as a check that your image runs and writes valid forecasts. **This run isn't ranked.** As with every Final run, you see its status, not its per-card details.

**After the close: the ranked run.** Every team's Final image then runs on a **fresh set of cards built after submissions close**, from data up to **Friday 23 October** (the last US close before the window ends):
- UST and G10 FX series, horizons of 2 to 12 business days, all four families;
- every target date falls between **27 October and 10 November**, after the cards are built;
- each card's family and wording come from fixed rules, so no window is chosen knowing whether a shock happened;
- an F4 card is one whose text corpus carries a live risk channel or a scheduled event inside the window; it doesn't promise that a shock happens.

The cards have the same files as the practice units, as described on #20. The ranked run uses the limits in the [Final limits notice](https://github.com/Agenthon-2026/Agenthon2026-public/issues/2#issuecomment-6099955125): 1,800 seconds per unit and 24 hours for the whole run. Scoring is the same rule as Development: each component divided by the error M0 expects on that card, scores clipped at 8.0, and an unscored card counts 8.0.

**Keep your image pullable until results are published on 13 November.** The ranked run, and our verification of the top entries after it, pull your image after the close.

**Results.** Provisional standings from **28 October**, updated as targets resolve. **Final results on 13 November.**

**What this replaces**
- README: the ranking is no longer "on the sealed set"; the sealed cards are used only for the check run.
- README, "Firewall": the "H2 2025 – Q2 2026" window and the EM FX bullet don't describe the ranked cards, and the F4 definition above replaces "Regime event labels for F4 cards".
- `docs/CATEGORIES.md`: in the Final, the F4 definition above replaces "The target window spans the shock's impact".
- README, website and CodaBench: verification doesn't happen within 13–25 October; we verify the top entries after their ranked runs, after the close.
- Our 7 and 10 October updates on Agenthon-2026/Agenthon2026-public#2: for Track 2, the image stays pullable until 13 November rather than 25 October, and provisional standings appear from 28 October rather than the Final board staying hidden until results are verified.

Questions are welcome here.

— The Agenthon 2026 organizers

@logxio, three of your four we can answer from the notice; the fourth is with the track lead.

1. **As-of:** yes, every ranked card shares one as-of, Friday 23 October.
2. **Windows:** 27 October – 10 November is the span of all target dates, not one window every card shares. In every family, a card's targets are 2 to 12 business days after the as-of, so they fall somewhere in that span.
3. **Assets:** UST and G10 FX series only, in all four families; no monthly, factor or EM FX assets.
4. **Whether the as-of panel includes 23 October's own close:** we've asked the track lead and will answer here as soon as we have it, aiming for before the Final opens on 13 October at 12:00 UTC.

— The Agenthon 2026 organizers

limits.body:
**Final run limits, all four tracks.** The Final + Verification phase opens on **13 October at 12:00 UTC** and closes on **25 October at 23:59 AoE**. These are the limits your one Final upload runs under. Where a value is the same as in Development, we say so; where it differs, the value here is the one the Final uses. We don't publish the number of Final units, or a bound on it.

**Every track**
- **One upload per team per track.** A Final upload that ends *Failed* doesn't use it, and you can upload again (as we said on Agenthon-2026/track1-coding-public#17). A held or cancelled upload does use it, and so does a run that gets scored.
- **One time allowance for the whole run: 24 hours** (86,400 s) to run your units, up from 12 hours in Development. Waiting in the queue before the run starts doesn't count, and scoring has its own clock. The 24 hours are shared by every unit in the run, so finish each unit as soon as you have an answer and cap your retries; one slow unit shouldn't spend time the rest of the run needs. On Tracks 1, 2 and 4, units the run hasn't started when the 24 hours end are recorded as `not_reached`: each scores as a failed unit and stays in the average, and the run is still scored, as in Development.
- **On Tracks 1, 2 and 4, your image is pulled once, before the first unit,** and that pull counts against the 24 hours. If it fails, each unit tries to pull the image again, and a unit that still can't scores `image_unusable`. That run is scored, so it uses your Final upload. Our 7 October update said such a run fails; this is the correct rule. So keep the image pullable until 25 October at 23:59 AoE.
- **Image checks:** pinned by digest, built for `linux/amd64`, with `LABEL qfbench2.interface_version="2.0"`, and no Docker `VOLUME`. An image that declares a `VOLUME` is marked *Failed* when its run starts and doesn't use your upload.
- **Outputs and logs are hidden** in the Final. You see your run's status, not its per-unit details, and the Final board stays hidden until results are verified and published.

**Tracks 1, 2 and 4 (House model tracks)**
- **Per unit:** a 16-CPU quota, 128 GiB RAM and a GPU, the same as Development.
- **Network:** only the House route; any other connection is refused and logged.
- **House model:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`, the same as in Development. Its **context window is 262,144 tokens**, read from the model server itself. (`docs/HOUSE-MODEL.md` lists the same number as tokenizer metadata and notes that the metadata alone doesn't set the window; this does.) A request whose prompt plus its output limit doesn't fit is refused before admission and doesn't count against your 25.
- **House requests:** 25 admitted requests per unit, at most 4,000 output tokens per request; admitted failures and retries count. There's no per-unit token allowance.
- **Output:** 64 MiB per file and 64 MiB in total per unit, with the same output-folder rules as Development.

**Track 1 (Coding).** Each unit has its own time limit, `[agent].timeout_sec` in that unit's `card.toml`, which your program can read in `/input` as in Development. In the Final it's **between 600 and 2,400 seconds** (10 to 40 minutes), depending on the unit. That's lower than many Development cards (1,200 to 5,400 seconds), so read the value from the card; don't carry over a Development number. In Development we suggested dividing the 12 hours by the number of units. That doesn't work in the Final, because the count isn't published: keep each unit inside its own limit, and finish early where you can, since the 24 hours are shared.

**Track 2 (Forecasting).** **1,800 seconds per unit**, as in Development. The Final cards set no timeout, so the launcher's default applies.

**Track 4 (Explainability).** **600 seconds per unit**, as in Development. The Final is scored with scorer 5.3.0, which Development has used since 9 October: the NLI judge checks your claims, and only the first 20 claims about each entity are checked and counted. As the README says, in the Final a canary string anywhere in your output is scored as contamination.

**Track 3 (Simulation)**
- **300 seconds per run.** A run that reaches the limit is stopped. The unit then scores 0 and stays in the average, as with any run that fails because of the submission.
- **Five runs per unit,** back to back on the same host and the same scenario seed: a warm-up, then four counted runs. The unit's rate is the median of the four. Every run, the warm-up included, has to succeed with the same stable outputs and event count.
- **4 CPUs (a CFS quota, not pinned cores) and 16 GiB,** `runc`, no network.
- **256 MiB** per output file and 256 MiB in total, as in Development.
- Units run one at a time on one dedicated GPU machine, within the same 24-hour allowance for the whole run.

Questions go on your track's tracker.

— The Agenthon 2026 organizers
